title: Before/after pair metadata (meta.json, one per pair folder)
description: Only pair_id, shape, volume_cc, view, consent_ref and clothing reach the model: build_caption() in training/scripts/build_dataset.py reads exactly those (plus brand and profile) and must stay byte-identical to buildCustomModelPrompt() in lib/prompt.ts. placement, incision and the frame metrics are recorded for curation, stratification and evaluation only; adding one here never changes a caption.

pair_id.description: Unique ID, e.g. 'clinic01-0001'. Must match the folder name.

brand.description: Implant brand, if the clinic recorded it.

shape.description: Implant shape. 'unknown' when the clinic did not document it; never guessed.

volume_cc.description: Implant volume in cc. If left/right differ, record the average and note it.

months_post_op.description: Months between surgery and the 'after' photo. 3+ preferred (settled result).

clothing.description: What the subject is wearing in BOTH photos (pairs must match).

consent_ref.description: Reference to the signed clinic agreement + patient release covering AI training, e.g. 'clinic01-agreement-2026-05'. Pairs without this are rejected at ingest.

placement.description: Where the implant sits relative to the pectoral muscle. A real confound: submuscular vs subglandular changes upper-pole shape at the same volume. From the chart only; 'unknown' when undocumented.

incision.description: Surgical approach. From the chart only; 'unknown' when undocumented.

height_cm.description: Patient height in centimetres. Frame metric: lets evaluation control for body type. Convert from the clinic's units; never estimated from the photo.

weight_kg.description: Patient weight in kilograms. Frame metric; see height_cm.

bra_size_before.description: Pre-operative bra size exactly as the clinic recorded it, e.g. '32B' or '10C (AU)'. Free text on purpose: sizing systems differ by market and are not normalised here.

chest_width_cm.description: Chest/base width in centimetres as measured at consultation. Frame metric; see height_cm.
